definitions: The calendar system currently used in most of the world, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582.
A solar calendar that defines a year of 365 days, with a leap day added every four years, except for years divisible by 100 but not by 400.
examples: The Gregorian calendar replaced the Julian calendar.
Most countries observe holidays according to the Gregorian calendar.
New Year's Day falls on January 1st in the Gregorian calendar.
